section_summary: This section (pages 81–160) consists primarily of State Department and Treasury Department correspondence, diplomatic notes exchanged with the Japanese Embassy, and internal memoranda between June and November 1941 concerning Japanese officials, language officers, researchers, and technical experts in the United States. The predominant administrative subject is the granting of reciprocal Federal income tax exemptions under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code and the expedited issuance of sailing permits and exit documents for Japanese nationals departing the country. The records also document the closure of the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office in New York in August 1941, the movement and surveillance of Japanese Foreign Office personnel travelling through the Americas, and compliance inquiries under the Alien Registration and Foreign Agents Registration Acts as bilateral relations deteriorated prior to the outbreak of the Pacific War.

subfiles.about: Acknowledges State Department certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Dr. Tatuzi Ito, granting Federal income tax exemption.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John L. Sullivan)
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges receipt of the State Department's letter of June 10, 1941, certifying that Dr. Tatuzi Ito, Professor of Niigata Medical University pursuing studies at New York University, is eligible for Federal income tax exemption. The letter notes that Dr. Ito plans to sail from San Francisco on June 20 aboard the steamship Nitta Maru. It confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Tax Exemption for Dr. Tatuzi Ito

subfiles.about: Requests Federal income tax exemption for Tyuhei Nakayama, Assistant Naval Engineer at the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office in New York.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests that Mr. Tyuhei Nakayama, a Japanese national attached to the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office in New York City as Assistant Naval Engineer, be granted exemption from Federal income taxes. The note states that Nakayama arrived in Seattle on April 18, 1941, aboard the steamship Heian Maru and that his compensation is derived solely from the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 147 Regarding Tax Exemption for Tyuhei Nakayama

subfiles.about: Certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Tyuhei Nakayama is eligible for Federal income tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits to the Secretary of the Treasury a copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 147 concerning Tyuhei Nakayama of the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office in New York City. The Secretary certifies, pursuant to Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, that Japan grants an equivalent exemption to United States Government employees performing services in Japan and that their official services are of similar character.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Tax Exemption for Tyuhei Nakayama
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 147 concerning the tax exemption of Tyuhei Nakayama and states it has been referred to Treasury authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 147 of June 4, 1941, regarding the tax exemption of Tyuhei Nakayama of the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office in New York City. The note states that a copy was transmitted to the competent authority of the United States Government with a view to granting tax exemption on his official compensation.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Tyuhei Nakayama

subfiles.about: Confirms that instructions will be issued granting Federal income tax exemption to Tyuhei Nakayama following State Department certification.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the Secretary of State's letter of June 10, 1941, enclosing Japanese Embassy Note No. 147 concerning Tyuhei Nakayama of the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office in New York. Treasury confirms that based on the State Department's Section 116(h) certification, appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Tyuhei Nakayama

subfiles.about: Addresses the refund of a $35.79 tax bond deposited by Jiro Tachibana with the Collector of Internal Revenue in New York upon his departure.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury responds to State Department inquiries regarding a Japanese Embassy note requesting the refund of a $35.79 bond deposited by Jiro Tachibana upon leaving New York on April 23, 1941. Treasury assumes the bond was deposited with the Collector of Internal Revenue at the New York Customhouse and confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued regarding the refund pursuant to earlier Section 116(h) certification.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Refund of Tax Bond for Jiro Tachibana

subfiles.about: Informs the Department of State of the scheduled departure from San Francisco of Mitsuo Okubo and requests tax exemption and a sailing permit.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador notifies the Secretary of State that Mitsuo Okubo, a clerk attached to the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office in New York City, will depart the United States. Having entered at Seattle on June 10, 1939, Okubo plans to sail from San Francisco on July 5, 1941, aboard the steamship Kamakura Maru, and requests that his sailing permit be issued in San Francisco. A duplicate copy of the first page of the note is preserved in the file.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 175 Regarding Departure and Tax Exemption of Mitsuo Okubo

subfiles.about: Transmits notification of the departure of Japanese official Mitsuo Okubo for the records of the Division of Alien Registration.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits information to the Attorney General referring to the Foreign Official Status Notification form submitted by Mitsuo Okubo, an official of the Japanese Government. The Department notes that Okubo was scheduled to depart the United States from San Francisco on July 5, 1941, aboard the steamship Kamakura Maru, and that a duplicate form was forwarded to the Division of Alien Registration.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Attorney General Regarding Departure of Mitsuo Okubo

subfiles.about: Confirms telephoned certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for tax exemption of Mitsuo Okubo.
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of State Sumner Welles confirms a telephone message of July 2, 1941, to the Bureau of Internal Revenue regarding tax exemption for Mitsuo Okubo of the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office in New York City. Welles provides formal certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code regarding reciprocal tax exemption for government employees, noting Okubo's planned sailing on July 5 from San Francisco on the Kamakura Maru.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Mitsuo Okubo
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Japanese Embassy Note No. 175 concerning tax exemption and sailing arrangements for Mitsuo Okubo.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 175 of June 30, 1941, regarding Mitsuo Okubo of the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office in New York. The note confirms that the information was communicated by telephone to competent authorities to facilitate Okubo's tax exemption prior to his departure from San Francisco.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Mitsuo Okubo

subfiles.about: Informs the Secretary of State of the scheduled departure from New York of Shiro Suzuki, an expert with the Japanese Government Raw Silk Bureau.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador notifies the State Department that Shiro Suzuki, an expert attached to the Japanese Government Raw Silk Bureau at 261 Fifth Avenue in New York City, will depart the United States. Having arrived on February 20, 1941, Suzuki is scheduled to sail from New York on July 15 aboard the steamship Tosan Maru, requesting that his sailing permit be issued in New York.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 176 Regarding Departure and Tax Exemption of Shiro Suzuki

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Japanese Embassy Note No. 176 concerning tax exemption for Shiro Suzuki of the Raw Silk Bureau.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 176 of June 30, 1941, concerning Shiro Suzuki of the Japanese Government Raw Silk Bureau in New York. The Secretary notes that the information was communicated by telephone to appropriate authorities to grant tax exemption on his official compensation prior to departure.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Shiro Suzuki

subfiles.about: Certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Shiro Suzuki of the Raw Silk Bureau.
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of State Sumner Welles confirms a telephone call of July 3, 1941, to the Bureau of Internal Revenue regarding tax exemption for Shiro Suzuki of the Japanese Government Raw Silk Bureau in New York. Welles provides formal certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, noting Suzuki's scheduled departure from New York on July 12 aboard the steamship Tosan Maru.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Shiro Suzuki
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: Confirms that instructions will be issued regarding tax exemption for Mitsuo Okubo following State Department certification.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John L. Sullivan)
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of July 11, 1941, certifying tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Mitsuo Okubo of the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office in New York. Treasury notes Okubo's planned sailing on July 5 from San Francisco on the Kamakura Maru and confirms instructions will be sent to the relevant Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Mitsuo Okubo

subfiles.about: Confirms instructions to Internal Revenue officials granting tax exemption to Shiro Suzuki of the Raw Silk Bureau.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of July 15, 1941, concerning Federal income tax exemption for Shiro Suzuki of the Japanese Government Raw Silk Bureau in New York. In response to the Section 116(h) certification, Treasury reports that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Shiro Suzuki

subfiles.about: Informs the Department of State of the departure and requests tax exemptions and sailing permits for Japanese Navy language officers Okada and Yamada.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador notifies the Secretary of State that Lieutenant Commander Sadatomo Okada and Lieutenant Wataru Yamada, language officers of the Imperial Japanese Navy residing in Washington, D.C., are departing the United States. The officers are scheduled to sail from San Francisco on July 5, 1941, aboard the Kamakura Maru and request that sailing permits be issued at San Francisco. Duplicate copies of the first page of the note are preserved in the file.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 179 Regarding Departure of Lieutenant Commander Sadatomo Okada and Lieutenant Wataru Yamada

subfiles.about: Certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Japanese Navy language officers Okada and Yamada, with a special note on their departure at State Department instance.
keywords: departure at instance of State Department
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of State Sumner Welles confirms a July 1 telephone message to the Bureau of Internal Revenue regarding tax exemption for Japanese Navy language officers Lieutenant Commander Sadatomo Okada and Lieutenant Wataru Yamada. Welles certifies reciprocal exemption under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, noting in an internal marginal memorandum that the standard clause asserting similarity of services was omitted at the request of the Far Eastern Division because the two officers departed at the instance of the State Department.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Sadatomo Okada and Wataru Yamada
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Japanese Embassy Note No. 179 concerning tax exemption for Lieutenant Commander Okada and Lieutenant Yamada.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges the receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 179 dated July 1, 1941, regarding the tax exemption of naval officers Sadatomo Okada and Wataru Yamada. The Secretary informs the Ambassador that the information was communicated by telephone to the competent United States authorities to grant the exemption prior to their departure.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Sadatomo Okada and Wataru Yamada

subfiles.about: Confirms instructions to Internal Revenue officials regarding tax exemption for Japanese language officers Okada and Yamada.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of July 14, 1941, certifying tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Lieutenant Commander Sadatomo Okada and Lieutenant Wataru Yamada. Treasury confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials regarding the two officers, who planned to sail from San Francisco on the Kamakura Maru.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Sadatomo Okada and Wataru Yamada

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note concerning inquiries to the Japanese Embassy about registration forms under the Registration Acts for exempt officials.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet references a note dated June 11, 1941, sent to the Japanese Embassy regarding various Registration Acts approved by Congress between 1917 and 1940. The note requested information from the Japanese Embassy as to whether notification forms had been forwarded covering all Japanese Government officials on whose behalf exemption was claimed, cross-referenced to file 800.01B11 Regis. Koike, Yachio/3.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note Regarding Japanese Officials Covered by Registration Acts

subfiles.about: Certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Paul Wikawa, assisting Assistant Military Attaché Colonel Hideo Iwakuro.
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of State Sumner Welles confirms a July 26 telephone call to the Bureau of Internal Revenue regarding tax exemption for Paul Wikawa, a secretary in the Japanese Foreign Office assisting Colonel Hideo Iwakuro, Assistant Military Attaché. Welles certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Wikawa, who plans to accompany Colonel Iwakuro sailing from San Francisco on July 31, 1941, aboard the Tatuta Maru.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Paul Wikawa
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: Notifies the State Department of the departure of Dr. Tatuzi Ito, Professor of Niigata Medical University, and requests tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador informs the Secretary of State that Dr. Tatuzi Ito, Professor of Niigata Medical University studying at New York University's Medical Department, is returning to Japan. Dr. Ito, who arrived in New York aboard the Kirishima Maru on November 28, 1939, is scheduled to depart San Francisco on June 20, 1941, on the Nitta Maru, requesting that his sailing permit be issued at San Francisco.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 146 Regarding Departure and Tax Exemption of Dr. Tatuzi Ito

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Japanese Embassy Note No. 146 concerning Dr. Tatuzi Ito and confirms arrangements for his tax clearance in San Francisco.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 146 of June 4, 1941, regarding the tax exemption and departure of Dr. Tatuzi Ito. The Secretary confirms that the information was telephoned to competent United States authorities to grant tax exemption and arrange for Dr. Ito to receive his sailing document at San Francisco prior to boarding the Nitta Maru.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Dr. Tatuzi Ito

subfiles.about: Confirms tax exemption instructions for Paul Wikawa, assistant to Colonel Hideo Iwakuro, sailing on the Tatuta Maru.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of July 30, 1941, certifying tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Paul Wikawa, secretary in the Japanese Foreign Office assisting Colonel Hideo Iwakuro. It notes that Wikawa plans to accompany Colonel Iwakuro sailing from San Francisco on July 31 aboard the Tatuta Maru, and confirms instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Paul Wikawa

subfiles.about: Confirms telephoned certification under Section 116(h) for tax exemption of Dr. Tatuzi Ito.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull confirms a telephone message of June 6, 1941, to the Bureau of Internal Revenue regarding tax exemption for Dr. Tatuzi Ito, Professor of Niigata Medical University studying at New York University. Hull formally certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, noting Dr. Ito's planned departure from San Francisco on June 20 aboard the Nitta Maru.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Dr. Tatuzi Ito
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: Reports that Mr. Anzorena of the Mexican Embassy stated a visa was granted to Japanese Foreign Office Extra-Secretary Yoshio Kobayashi for travel to Chile.
subfiles.summary: A memorandum from the Division of the American Republics records that Mr. Anzorena of the Mexican Embassy in Washington phoned to advise that a visa had been granted to Yoshio Kobayashi, described as an 'Extra Secretary' of the Japanese Foreign Office in Tokyo. Kobayashi stated that he planned to fly to Chile on June 27, 1941, on official business with no planned stopovers.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Regarding Chilean Visa Granted to Yoshio Kobayashi
subfiles.to: Mr. Kelchner / Division of the American Republics

subfiles.about: Instructs the American Embassy in Santiago to report on the movements and activities of Japanese Foreign Office official Yoshio Kobayashi.
subfiles.summary: In a confidential instruction sent by air mail, the Secretary of State informs the American Ambassador in Santiago of information received from the Mexican Embassy that Yoshio Kobayashi, an 'Extra Secretary' of the Japanese Foreign Office, departed by plane for Chile on official business. The Ambassador is requested to monitor and report to the State Department on Kobayashi's movements and activities.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 590 to the American Ambassador in Santiago Regarding Yoshio Kobayashi
subfiles.to: American Ambassador, Santiago, Chile (Claude G. Bowers)

subfiles.about: Cross-references a memorandum on the official closing of the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York as of August 7, 1941.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet records an August 11, 1941 State Department memorandum by F. C. Lyon concerning the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York. The note indicates that the office was officially closed on August 7, 1941, and that retained records were transferred to the Japanese Consulate General in New York, cross-referencing file 701.9411/1443.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note Regarding the Closing of the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York

subfiles.about: Details intelligence reports regarding the closure of the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York, departure of personnel, and disposition of records and funds.
subfiles.from: Commander H. E. Keisker, USNR (Office of Naval Intelligence)
subfiles.summary: Commander H. E. Keisker of the Office of Naval Intelligence forwards information from the Commandant of the Third Naval District stating that the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office at 1 Madison Avenue in New York officially closed on August 7, 1941. The memorandum notes that Engineer Captain Yuzo Ishikawa and Paymaster Commander Kanegoro Koike flew to the West Coast to sail on the Asama Maru, that clerk Ryuzo Mishima remained to wind up affairs, unimportant records were burned while important files were sent to the Consulate General, and bank funds were transferred to Riggs National Bank in Washington to the account of Naval Attaché Captain Ichiro Yokoyama.
subfiles.title: Office of Naval Intelligence Memorandum on the Closing of the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York

subfiles.about: Informs Dr. Tatuzi Ito that his inquiry regarding departure documents was referred to the Bureau of Internal Revenue.
subfiles.from: Department of State (For the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: The Department of State acknowledges a letter of February 26, 1941, from Dr. Tatuzi Ito regarding his desire to obtain clearance documents for departure from New York on or about March 8, 1941. The Department advises Dr. Ito that the Bureau of Internal Revenue received a copy of his request and is preparing an appropriate reply directly to him.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Department of State to Dr. Tatuzi Ito Regarding Sailing Document

subfiles.about: Requests tax exemption and an expedited sailing permit for Misao Eguchi of the Formosan Government Commission.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador informs the Secretary of State of the departure of Misao Eguchi, Administrative Secretary to the Formosan Government Commission located at 350 Fifth Avenue (Empire State Building), New York City. Eguchi plans to sail from Los Angeles on September 20 aboard the steamship Thomson and urgently requests his sailing permit in New York by noon on September 15.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 270 Regarding Departure and Tax Exemption of Misao Eguchi

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Japanese Embassy Note No. 270 concerning Misao Eguchi and confirms telephoned instructions for tax clearance.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 270 of September 12, 1941, concerning Misao Eguchi of the Formosan Government Commission. The note confirms that information was telephoned on September 12 to competent United States Government authorities to facilitate tax exemption and the issuance of a sailing document in New York prior to his departure from Los Angeles.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Misao Eguchi

subfiles.about: Confirms telephoned certification under Section 116(h) for tax exemption of Misao Eguchi of the Formosan Government Commission.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull confirms a telephone message of September 12, 1941, to the Bureau of Internal Revenue regarding tax exemption for Misao Eguchi, Administrative Secretary to the Formosan Government Commission in New York City. Hull certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, noting Eguchi's scheduled sailing from Los Angeles on September 20 aboard the steamship Thomson.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Misao Eguchi
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: Confirms that instructions will be issued regarding tax exemption for Misao Eguchi of the Formosan Government Commission.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of September 23, 1941, certifying tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Misao Eguchi of the Formosan Government Commission in New York. The Treasury confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials concerning Eguchi's sailing on the steamship Thomson.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Misao Eguchi

subfiles.about: Informs the Department of State of the departure of three Japanese Government Railways officials and requests tax exemption and sailing permits.
keywords: Department of Imperial Japanese Government Railways
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador informs the Secretary of State that Hirohiko Tembo, Yasushi Obata, and Seishi Ohtsuka, attached to the New York Office of the Department of Imperial Japanese Government Railways at 630 Fifth Avenue, are returning to Japan. The Ambassador requests that their names be submitted to appropriate authorities for tax exemption and the issuance of sailing permits in New York for departure on the earliest possible ship.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 279 Regarding Departure of Hirohiko Tembo, Yasushi Obata, and Seishi Ohtsuka

subfiles.about: Confirms certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for tax exemption of three Japanese Government Railways officials.
keywords: Department of Imperial Japanese Government Railways
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull confirms a telephone message of September 23, 1941, to the Bureau of Internal Revenue regarding tax exemption for Hirohiko Tembo, Yasushi Obata, and Seishi Ohtsuka of the Imperial Japanese Government Railways New York office. Hull certifies reciprocal tax exemption pursuant to Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, noting the officials wish to depart as soon as possible and obtain sailing documents in New York.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Hirohiko Tembo, Yasushi Obata, and Seishi Ohtsuka
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Japanese Embassy Note No. 279 and confirms telephoned instructions regarding tax clearance for the three railways officials.
keywords: Department of Imperial Japanese Government Railways
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 279 of September 22, 1941, regarding the tax exemption and departure of Hirohiko Tembo, Yasushi Obata, and Seishi Ohtsuka of the Japanese Government Railways. The note states that the information was communicated by telephone to the competent United States authorities to exempt their compensation from Federal income tax and facilitate sailing documents in New York.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Hirohiko Tembo, Yasushi Obata, and Seishi Ohtsuka

subfiles.about: Confirms that instructions will be issued granting tax exemption to three Japanese Government Railways officials.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of September 30, 1941, certifying tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Hirohiko Tembo, Yasushi Obata, and Seishi Ohtsuka of the Imperial Japanese Government Railways New York office. Treasury states that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials concerned.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Hirohiko Tembo, Yasushi Obata, and Seishi Ohtsuka

subfiles.about: Cross-references a memorandum comparing departure documents required of citizens by the U.S. Government versus those required by Japan.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet references a memorandum dated September 16, 1941, prepared in the Division of Far Eastern Affairs by Mr. Schuler. The subject concerns a comparison of documents required by the United States Government of Japanese nationals leaving the country versus documents required by Japan of American citizens leaving Japan, cross-referenced to file E 894.56/82.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note Regarding Travel Documents Required by the U.S. and Japanese Governments

subfiles.about: Informs the Department of State of the scheduled departure of Shigeyoshi Obata, Extra-Secretary of the Foreign Office assisting the Ambassador.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador informs the Secretary of State that Shigeyoshi Obata, Extra-Secretary of the Japanese Foreign Office residing at the Ambassador's residence, will depart the United States. Obata, who arrived in San Francisco on January 10, 1941, on the Nitta Maru, plans to sail from San Francisco on November 2 aboard the Tatuta Maru and requests that his sailing permit be issued in Washington, D.C.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 297 Regarding Departure and Tax Exemption of Shigeyoshi Obata

subfiles.about: Explains that diplomatic embassy personnel like Shigeyoshi Obata do not fall under Section 116(h) and outlines proper clearance procedure.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State responds to Japanese Embassy Note No. 297 concerning Shigeyoshi Obata, confirming an October 21 telephone conversation. The Department clarifies that Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code applies only to consular and non-diplomatic officials, not embassy staff, and advises that Obata should present an embassy letter bearing the official seal and his passport directly to the Bureau of Internal Revenue to obtain his sailing document.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Departure Procedures for Shigeyoshi Obata

subfiles.about: Informs the State Department of the departure of Motonaga Ohto of the Raw Silk Bureau and requests tax exemption and a sailing permit.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador notifies the Secretary of State that Motonaga Ohto, Attaché to the Bureau of Trade in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry attached to the Japanese Government Raw Silk Bureau in New York, will depart the United States. Having arrived in San Francisco on November 2, 1938, Ohto plans to depart New York on October 25 to board the Tatuta Maru sailing from San Francisco on November 2, requesting his sailing permit in New York. A duplicate copy of the note follows on pages 141-142.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 302 Regarding Departure and Tax Exemption of Motonaga Ohto

subfiles.about: Confirms certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for tax exemption of Motonaga Ohto.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull confirms a telephone message of October 22, 1941, to the Bureau of Internal Revenue regarding tax exemption for Motonaga Ohto of the Japanese Government Raw Silk Bureau in New York. Hull certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, noting Ohto's travel to San Francisco to sail on November 2.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Motonaga Ohto
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Japanese Embassy Note No. 302 and confirms telephoned instructions regarding tax clearance for Motonaga Ohto.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 302 of October 21, 1941, regarding the tax exemption and departure of Motonaga Ohto of the Japanese Government Raw Silk Bureau. The note confirms that information was telephoned to competent United States authorities to exempt Ohto's official compensation from Federal income tax.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Motonaga Ohto

subfiles.about: Confirms instructions to Internal Revenue officials regarding tax exemption for Motonaga Ohto.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (John L. Sullivan)
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of November 1, 1941, confirming certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Motonaga Ohto of the Japanese Government Raw Silk Bureau. The Treasury notes Ohto's scheduled sailing from San Francisco on November 2 and confirms instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Motonaga Ohto

subfiles.about: Informs the Department of State of the departure of Foreign Office researchers Kiyohiko Turumi and Ryozo Sunobe and requests tax exemption and sailing permits.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador notifies the Secretary of State that Kiyohiko Turumi and Ryozo Sunobe, researchers of the Department of Foreign Affairs studying in the United States in preparation for diplomatic service at Williams College and Amherst College respectively, are returning to Japan. They are scheduled to depart Seattle on November 4, 1941, aboard the Hikawa Maru, and request sailing permits in Seattle. A duplicate copy of the first page is included in the file.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 309 Regarding Departure of Kiyohiko Turumi and Ryozo Sunobe

subfiles.about: Confirms certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for tax exemption of Kiyohiko Turumi and Ryozo Sunobe.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull confirms an October 29 telephone message to the Bureau of Internal Revenue regarding tax exemption for Foreign Office researchers Kiyohiko Turumi and Ryozo Sunobe. Hull certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, noting that the two researchers plan to sail from Seattle on November 4 aboard the Hikawa Maru.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Kiyohiko Turumi and Ryozo Sunobe
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Japanese Embassy Note No. 309 and confirms arrangements for tax exemption of Kiyohiko Turumi and Ryozo Sunobe.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 309 of October 27, 1941, regarding the departure and tax exemption of researchers Kiyohiko Turumi and Ryozo Sunobe. The note states that the information was communicated by telephone to the competent United States authorities to grant tax exemption on their official compensation prior to their departure from Seattle.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Kiyohiko Turumi and Ryozo Sunobe

subfiles.about: Informs the Department of State of the departure of Yaroku Katayama, Head of the Osaka Commercial Museum in New York, and requests tax clearance.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador notifies the Secretary of State that Yaroku Katayama, sent to the United States by the Japanese Government as Head of the Osaka Commercial Museum at 200 Madison Avenue in New York City, is returning to Japan. Katayama is scheduled to leave Seattle on November 4, 1941, on the steamship Hikawa Maru, and requests that his sailing permit be issued in Seattle. A duplicate copy follows on page 156.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 310 Regarding Departure and Tax Exemption of Yaroku Katayama

subfiles.about: Confirms certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for tax exemption of Yaroku Katayama.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull confirms a telephone message of October 31, 1941, to the Bureau of Internal Revenue regarding tax exemption for Yaroku Katayama, who has been in the United States on an official mission as head of the Osaka Commercial Museum. Hull certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, noting Katayama's planned departure from Seattle on November 4 aboard the Hikawa Maru.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Yaroku Katayama
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Japanese Embassy Note No. 310 and confirms telephoned instructions regarding tax clearance for Yaroku Katayama.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 310 of October 27, 1941, concerning the departure and tax exemption of Yaroku Katayama, head of the Osaka Commercial Museum in New York City. The Secretary informs the Ambassador that the information was communicated by telephone to the competent United States authorities to grant tax exemption on Katayama's official compensation and facilitate his sailing document at Seattle.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Yaroku Katayama
